How do I maximize GPU utilization when training small LLMs on an RTX 3060 with 6GB VRAM?

To maximize an RTX 3060 6GB VRAM GPU when training small LLMs:
1. Use Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) with LoRA or QLoRA.
2. Enable gradient checkpointing in PyTorch to trade compute for memory.
3. Set per_device_train_batch_size=1 and use gradient_accumulation_steps=8 to simulate an effective batch size of 8 without OOM.
4. Use 16-bit mixed precision (fp16 or bf16) or 4-bit/8-bit quantized base models.
5. Cap your max_seq_length to 512 or 1024 tokens during training.

What is the core difference between pre-training and fine-tuning an LLM?

Pre-training is the foundational stage where a neural network learns general language patterns, syntax, logic, and factual world knowledge by predicting the next token over trillions of words (requiring hundreds to thousands of server GPUs). Fine-tuning takes that pre-trained model and adjusts a small fraction of its weights on specialized data (using techniques like LoRA on a single consumer GPU) to adapt its tone, format, domain knowledge, or instruction-following behavior.

LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) freezes the billions of original weights of a foundation model and inserts small, low-rank trainable adapter matrices next to the attention layers. Instead of updating 8 billion parameters, LoRA only trains around 0.1% to 1% (a few million parameters). This drastically reduces VRAM requirements and training time while retaining nearly all the performance of full fine-tuning.
